Actual Article Body:

It's a busy late night in Canberra's city centre. Patrons are crisscrossing the road in the city interchange, wandering from one club to another.

Login or signup to continue reading

Police sirens wail in pursuit as a car with one wheel missing scrapes its way through Alinga Street.

Business owner John-Paul Romano is recording the scene, pausing between customers because wild as Civic may be sometimes, you don't see this every night.

As co-owner and operator of hot dog joint The Doghouse, Mr Romano has found himself an unlikely documentarian of the scenes and characters of Canberra's nightlife.

Mr Romano describes the business, started in March 2025, as a side hustle.

By day he works for a police union and has an earlier history in hospitality, having owned a bar through the pandemic.

From 10pm on Thursday to Saturday nights, Mr Romano and business partner Daniel Elix serve hot dogs from borrowed space at the front of the bakery which supplies their buns.

Soon after launch they started documenting their nights on social media, and soon their accounts took off.

"You can hear them when they walk past, saying, 'that's the place from Instagram, that's the place from TikTok'," he said.

Mr Romano describes their online accounts as a modern version of the social pages. They certainly have a wide reach, reporting more than 6.5 million views in the past three months.

Amid the countless photos of young bar-goers, The Doghouse has served and photographed cross-section of Canberra, including MLAs. Mr Romano tries to post as many photos as possible, unedited. He says it's a raw account of Canberra nightlife, and his library is now more than 50,000 pictures.

Fights aren't uncommon in the city and more than a few of them have played out in front of Mr Romano's camera. Most, however, are kept offline.

"What we're documenting is a history in real time of Canberra's nightlife and I think anyone would be remiss to say that altercations don't occur amongst nightclub precincts," he said.

Mr Romano still generally describes the city environment as safe, welcoming and inclusive. He reports a tight-knit community among nightlife patrons, staff and business owners.
